html:
Madagascar is the world's fourth-largest island, in the Indian Ocean off south-east Africa. The map shows it from 1000 to the present, first as a land of many peoples and kingdoms, then as a French colony and an independent country.

Its people came from two directions. Sailors from the islands of Southeast Asia, probably from southern Borneo, crossed the ocean in the first millennium CE, the Austronesian settlement of Madagascar. Bantu-speaking Africans came from the mainland. The Malagasy language is Austronesian, closest to languages of Borneo, while many words and customs are African. Rice paddies sit beside herds of zebu cattle.

The island's history in brief:

  • From the 1000s Swahili and Arab traders ran ports in the north-west.
  • From the 1500s kingdoms grew: the Sakalava in the west, the Betsimisaraka in the east, and the Merina in the central highlands.
  • Around 1700 pirates used the east coast as a base.
  • In the 1800s the Merina kings, ruling from the Rova of Antananarivo, conquered most of the island and allied with Britain.
  • France invaded in 1895 and made it a colony in 1896. A great uprising against French rule in 1947 was crushed with heavy loss of life.
  • It became independent in 1960.

Since then the country has seen several coups and political crises and remains one of the poorest in the world. Most of its plants and animals, such as lemurs, live nowhere else, and much of its forest has been cut down.
sum: Madagascar is the world's fourth-largest island, in the Indian Ocean off south-east Africa. The map shows it from 1000 to the present, first as a land of many peoples and kingdoms, then as a French colony and an independent country.
